meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

meanings.note: clear liquid soup made by boiling meat or vegetables

examples.trans: The broth is simmering quietly on the stove.

examples.text: Главное, не пересоли бульон на плите.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not oversalt the broth on the stove.

examples.text: Бульон уже сварился для этого соуса?

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'купить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'bought out'.

examples.text: Я выкупил вторую половину ресторана у Кристины.
examples.trans: I bought out the second half of the restaurant from Kristina.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и выкупить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and bought out on time.

meanings.note: Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'grandfather' in everyday Russian.
Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'grandfather' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: My grandfather was a partisan for three years!
My grandfather lives in the country.

examples.text: Я никого пытать не буду, ясно? У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: I'm not going to torture anyone, got it? My grandfather was a partisan for three years!

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.

meanings.note: large structure such as an office, school, or hall

examples.text: На огромной скорости машина врезалась в здание!

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание!

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: As you all know...
I don't know.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'of Ilyich' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Only the apartment of Kirill Ilyich remained.

examples.text: Ну правильно, это квартира для Макса.
examples.trans: That is right, this apartment is for Max.

examples.text: Кирилл Ильич, ну что ты начинаешь?
examples.trans: Kirill Ilyich, why are you starting this?

meanings.note: Also a flat number in an address. Common feminine noun meaning 'flat, apartment' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Kirill' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('chicken (relational)').

meanings.note: Culinary. Common neuter noun meaning 'meat' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?

But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need a job too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'лить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'poured over / drenched'.

examples.trans: He poured soup all over me.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и облить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and poured over on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'острение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'flare-up, relapse' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right now she is having a seasonal flare-up.

examples.text: Ей нельзя нервничать, у неё обострение!
examples.trans: She must not get nervous, she is having a flare-up!

examples.text: Какое ещё у тебя обострение, дочка?
examples.trans: What kind of flare-up are you having, daughter?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I'll explain everything later.
Explain, please.
I will explain everything to you right now.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat.
An excellent area!

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: 'по поводу' + genitive. Common masculine noun meaning 'reason, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm calling about the shopping centre.
It's a good occasion.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лчаса'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half an hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The sauce was ordered half an hour ago.
The sauce was ordered a whole half-hour ago.

examples.text: Ты моешь её уже целых полчаса.
examples.trans: You have been washing it for a whole half hour already.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.trans: I made a cake.
Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to attempt', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.trans: I tried!
He tried to explain the situation.

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'купить'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bought up / sold out').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень раскупить выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very bought up choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто раскупить день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply bought up day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: Hot liquid dish. Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
See you tomorrow!
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
